titleText.es: Nunca vemos viajeros en el tiempo porque todos descubren que es un gran error. Esto también es la causa por la que hae poco tu amigo del laboratorio de pronto empezó a parecer un año más viejo.
titleText.en: We never see any time travelers because they all discover it's a huge mistake. This is also why your friend at the lab suddenly looked about a year older recently.
titleText.noteEn: Both title attributes are preserved exactly; the Spanish archive really prints the typo hae where standard Spanish would use hace. The visible raster localizes the official impact sound WHAM as PLUM. OCR hallucinated 2517 from drawing strokes on the workbench, omitted the panel-two ¿SÍ? and the last-panel ¿QUÉ HAY?, read PLUM as puM and the last HOLA as QUE, dropped the I from IDEA, and misread GUAU, TÚ, and accented ALGÚN.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Guau can express surprise or admiration. The same spelling can imitate a dog's bark in a different setting.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; part of estar a punto de
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A belongs to the fixed pattern estar a punto de, which says that an action is just about to happen.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; part of estar a punto de
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Punto usually means ‘point,’ but within estar a punto de it helps form the meaning ‘be about to.’

example.es: El tren está a punto de llegar.
example.en: The train is about to arrive.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; links estar a punto to the imminent action
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In estar a punto de, de is required immediately before the action verb in its unchanged -ar, -er, or -ir form.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: really?; is that so? (asking for confirmation)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sí normally means ‘yes.’ Said as a short question, it can echo surprising information and ask the other person to confirm it.
Plum is sound-imitating writing used for a sudden heavy impact or fall.
Sucede is a present form of suceder for one event or situation. It says that the event happens or takes place.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins más o menos
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Más, o, and menos combine as más o menos to mean ‘more or less,’ ‘roughly,’ or ‘approximately.’

example.es: Tarda más o menos una hora.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; middle of más o menos
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Más, o, and menos combine as más o menos to mean ‘more or less,’ ‘roughly,’ or ‘approximately.’

example.es: Llegarán más o menos a las ocho.
example.en: They will arrive at about eight.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; completes más o menos
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Más, o, and menos combine as más o menos to mean ‘more or less,’ ‘roughly,’ or ‘approximately.’

example.es: Son más o menos veinte personas.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In a frequency expression, al combines a + el before a masculine time period: una vez al mes means ‘once per month.’

example.es: Voy al médico dos veces al año.
example.en: I go to the doctor twice a year.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: estar a punto de + verbo en forma de diccionario
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that an action is just about to happen?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of estar, then a punto de, then the action verb in its unchanged -ar, -er, or -ir form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Only estar changes for the person and time: estoy, estás, está, and so on. A punto de stays together, and the following action verb remains unchanged. The plus sign means ‘followed by.’

example.es: La película está a punto de empezar.
example.en: The film is about to start.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you say that a number, time, or description is approximate?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use más o menos before or after the approximate information.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The literal pieces are ‘more or less,’ but together they often work like ‘roughly,’ ‘about,’ or ‘approximately.’

example.es: El viaje dura más o menos dos horas.
example.en: The trip takes about two hours.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: una vez al + período de tiempo
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something happens once in each stated time period?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use una vez al before a masculine time period, such as día, mes, or año.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Una vez supplies ‘once.’ Al is a + el and introduces the repeating period. With a feminine period, use a la instead, as in una vez a la semana.

example.es: La reunión ocurre una vez al año.
example.en: The meeting happens once a year.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: máquina del tiempo · yo futuro · impedir la idea · una vez al mes
cardDefinitions.questionEn: What time-travel loop creates the joke?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: A future Rob travels back to stop his earlier self from inventing a time machine, hits him with a bat, and takes his place. The caption suggests that versions of this self-intervention happen to would-be inventors somewhere roughly once a month.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Earlier Rob recognizes the visitor as his future self. Future Rob says the invention idea is imminent and stops it with the bat, creating a causal paradox: the trip depends on the time machine whose invention he prevents. In the final panel the older visitor has taken earlier Rob's place and hidden the bat behind the desk; the official title text's suddenly older lab friend points to that replacement. The caption generalizes the episode rather than saying that the same man repeats it monthly.
